result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers assign all ten events a treatment and handle the urgent, nothing-happened and promotional cases well. A wins mainly on the automatic rebooking: it says the message should show the old flight and the new flight, with an undo or 'call a person' option, while B only calls it top priority. B's three-group toggles are a slightly lighter way to let users adjust alerts than A's five kinds, but A's per-notification feedback and its 'keep safety alerts?' prompt largely make up for that. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give all ten events a clear treatment and handle the no-news and promotional messages well. B pulls ahead on the automatic rebooking: its message shows the old flight, the new flight, and an undo or 'call a person' option, while A only calls it top priority. B also keeps cancellation and payment alerts on their own switch so users who mute everything still get them, which directly answers the opt-out concern.
